title: Integration test harness: mid-upgrade failure injection + rollback restores health within SLO
author: Leila Farouk
release_notes: Internal: adds an integration test harness that simulates a mid-upgrade failure and verifies rollback returns the deployment to healthy within the target recovery time; runs in CI on main.
description:
Context: We’ve added upgrade planning, prechecks, backups, and rollback hooks, but we didn’t have a deterministic end-to-end test that proves the system can recover when an upgrade fails mid-flight. This PR adds an integration test harness that (a) spins up a disposable Kubernetes cluster, (b) installs a known-good baseline of Redwood Private, (c) performs an upgrade with an injected failure after the “point of no return” guardrails are evaluated but before the full system is healthy, and (d) executes rollback and verifies service health is restored within a target time window.

What’s included (high level): 1) A new integration harness under tests/integration/ that provisions a KinD cluster, installs a baseline release, and runs the installer CLI commands end-to-end. 2) Failure injection helpers that simulate realistic mid-upgrade breakages (kill migration job, fail an image pull, or force an unhealthy rollout) without requiring custom images. 3) Health verification: ensures control plane + gateway become Ready, and validates the control plane health endpoint is reachable via port-forward; also checks that component versions match the “previous known good” baseline after rollback. 4) Diagnostics on failure: if the test fails, we automatically collect installer diagnostics (precheck report, step timings, k8s events, and pod logs) and upload as a CI artifact. 5) CI wiring: GitHub Actions job that runs this suite on PRs touching upgrade/rollback code paths, and always on main.

SLO/targets: The test enforces that rollback restores overall service health within 8 minutes (configurable via IT_ROLLBACK_TARGET_SECONDS). This is aligned with the Private beta runbook expectations for a typical maintenance window rehearsal.

How it works: - Cluster bring-up: KinD v1.29 with a storage class suitable for snapshot tests (we skip PV snapshot coverage here; that stays in dedicated backup tests). - Baseline install: installs chart set pinned to BASELINE_BUNDLE (defaults to the last release candidate in ci/fixtures). - Upgrade attempt: runs `rpi upgrade apply` using the upgrade bundle built in CI, with `--non-interactive` and step-level timeouts. - Failure injection: after the backup step completes, the harness injects a failure (default: delete the control-plane migration Job pod once it starts, causing the upgrade gate to fail deterministically). - Rollback: runs `rpi rollback` and waits for readiness/health checks to pass; asserts the installer reports “rollback completed” and that the component version report matches baseline. - Cleanup: always tries to gather diagnostics before tearing down the cluster.

Notes/limitations: - This harness focuses on rollback correctness and recovery time. It does not attempt to validate data correctness after forward-only migrations; those cases are expected to block rollback earlier via compatibility checks. - We keep runtime reasonable (~16–20 minutes in CI) by scoping the deployed footprint and using cached images where possible.

Follow-ups: - Add additional failure modes from the ENG-2322 matrix (disk-full simulation and snapshot permission failure) once we’re happy with flake rates. - Consider a nightly job that runs the full matrix instead of gating every PR.

Test plan: - `make itest-upgrade-rollback` locally (requires Docker). - CI: `itest / upgrade-rollback (kind)` on PR and main.

Risk: Low. This adds new tests + CI wiring only; no production installer behavior changes.

test(integration): implement baseline install + health assertions

ci: add github actions workflow + artifact upload for diagnostics
docs: note integration test usage + env vars
conversation: Devon Price (review): This is the missing piece for confidence. A couple requests: (1) please ensure we always collect diagnostics even on timeout; (2) can we make the rollback target time configurable via env var so we can tune it per runner?

Leila Farouk (author): Done. Added a deferred diagnostics collection path that runs on any failure/timeout and uploads `diagnostics.tgz` in CI. Also added `IT_ROLLBACK_TARGET_SECONDS` with default 480s and surfaced it in the workflow + README.

Connor O'Brien (review): Can you clarify in the test what boundary we’re validating? Specifically: the failure should happen after backups complete and after at least one component upgrade begins, otherwise we’re just testing the happy-path rollback command. Also, please pin the baseline bundle so we don’t drift silently.

Leila Farouk (author): Updated the harness to wait for the backup step completion log marker before injecting the failure (we key off the step id from `upgrade apply --json`). Baseline is now pinned via `tests/integration/fixtures/baseline/version.txt` and validated at runtime before install.
Rafael Mendes (review): For supportability, can we emit the correlation id we used for the run as part of the test output? That helps when we compare with control-plane logs.
Leila Farouk (author): Added `IT_CORRELATION_ID` generation and print at start; also pass it into the installer env so logs include it consistently.
Aisha Bello (review): Concern: this will be noisy/flaky and slow for every PR. Can we gate it only when files in upgrade/rollback paths change, and run nightly otherwise?

Leila Farouk (author): Workflow now uses `paths` filters (installer upgrade/rollback packages + helm coordination + integration tests). For main we still run unconditionally; we can add a nightly matrix job in a follow-up.
Sean Gallagher (review): Please cap the cluster bring-up and wait loops; I don’t want a stuck KinD job burning runner hours. Also add explicit `kubectl get events` to diagnostics collection.
Leila Farouk (author): Added global job timeout (35m) and per-wait timeouts (e.g., 10m for rollout). Diagnostics now include `kubectl get events -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp` and node/pod summaries.
Devon Price (approval): Looks good now. Diagnostics capture is solid. Approving.
Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved. This aligns with ENG-2322 direction; let’s follow up with more failure modes once it stabilizes.
